I am not sure what method he is using that he uses his coffee maker, nor am I positive what he means by cannahoney as it could refer to a few different products but here is a quick run down of how to turn your weed into a concentrate that you can use as an edible or a smokeable. It will already be active so there is no need to decarb using this type of oil.

One thing you will need for this is 99% isopropyl alcohol, it must be that high of a percentage or you will be smoking byproducts. This should have been step 1 - put your isopropyl in the freezer for at least 4 hours beforehand.

Step 1 - make sure your weed is really dry, most weed is going to be cured perfectly which would mean not quite dry enough for an extract. You can skip this step, but a really dry product that almost crumbles will give you a better yield.

Step 2 - cut a 2 liter bottle in half, and use a nail to poke holes in all the lowest spots on the bottom of the bottle and put a coffee filter in the bottom half of the bottle and you can just throw away the top half.

Step 3 - you can throw your unchopped buds in the bottle, or you can grind or chop them and put them in the bottle. If your objective is strictly to get high and have the best tasting product, then don't chop or grind the bud. If your objective is medicinal purposes and you aren't too concerned with how it tastes when you smoke it, then I would chop or grind it. Chopping or grinding it will get more of the plant matter and more of the cannabinoids so it will be a much darker product. It can still be smoked but not recommended.

Step 4 - Get an old crockpot preferably or a rice cooker, but rice cookers tend to get a bit too hot. Pour the isopropyl over the weed, and have the liquid coming out the bottom of the bottle run into the crockpot. This step you can also make a decision about getting high or medicinal use. You can soak the weed in the isopropyl for a day if you want to soak out a lot of plant matter and have darker oil, which many argue is necessary for medical. I don't soak because I like a nice tasting, nice looking product and I just do a very quick rinse.

Step 5 - the reason we are using a crockpot or a rice cooker is because it's not safe to cook the alcohol out indoors. Take your crockpot or rice cooker and plug it in outside and turn it on low. This can take anywhere from 10 minutes to a few hours depending on how much you are making. From here you are simply cooking the alcohol off. You can tell when it's done because it won't smell like alcohol at all anymore, and instead will be what is in my opinion the best smell out there.
